title: metric-shard-allocator-and-log-rotation-orchestration
author: Maya Alvarez
description: Motivation: Private installs with many tenants were hitting Prometheus scrape cardinality ceilings and log retention costs spiking due to undifferentiated retention. This PR implements an automation layer that: 1) shards Prometheus storage and scrape responsibility by tenant grouping with a pluggable allocator; 2) wires a coordinated log-rotation and compression pipeline for fluentd/Vector with tenant-aware retention and lifecycle policies; 3) augments the Helm charts and Terraform modules to surface shard allocation, retention tiers, and safe-rollback hooks; and 4) extends the installer upgrade operator to run migration jobs in a replayable, checkpointed fashion so metric rebalancing is rollback-safe. Key goals: reduce peak TSDB size on single nodes, enable tenant isolation for SLO-aligned retention, provide deterministic rollbacks for schema/mapping changes, and keep private installs operable without manual shard reassignments. What this changes: - Terraform: new module observability/shard_allocator with inputs (tenant_selector, shard_count, region_affinity, retention_preset); automatic generation of PrometheusRule and ServiceMonitor bindings; state tracked in a Dynamo-compatible statestore in airgapped mode (optional). - Helm: chart updates to prometheus-operator subchart to accept shard labels and to deploy a small allocator controller as a Deployment; fluentd/Vector chart updated with lifecycle hooks, compression sidecar, and rotation policy CRDs. - Installer operator: upgrade plan steps now include preflight allocation dry-run, migration job (checkpointed), post-migration validation probes, and rollback reversal plan which replays inverse migration steps. - Migration tooling: small Ruby/Go migration job image that can replay sample metrics re-ingestion with idempotency tokens. - Dashboards/Alerts: Grafana folder templating to create per-shard dashboards, new alert generator templates for shard imbalance and retention anomalies. - Tests: integration test harness in perf-canary that simulates 1k tenants and validates shard assignment convergence and rollback correctness. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and example usage - [x] Helm chart changes with smoke charts - [x] Installer operator hooks and tests - [x] Migration job image and idempotency - [x] Grafana folder templating and example dashboards - [x] CI integration and perf-canary scenario Notes and tradeoffs: Sharding adds operational surface area; allocator defaults aim for conservative shard counts to avoid short-lived reassignments. In airgapped installs the statestore uses an on-cluster CRD-backed object rather than external Dynamo. Related: ENG-4121 (prometheus-ttl-strategy), PRs for prometheus-operator compatibility, and an upcoming RFC on tenant retention tiers. Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature flag "obs_shard_allocator" in the installer config; gradual rollout per-customer with canary set and verification probes.

release_notes: Added an optional Prometheus shard allocator and coordinated log rotation/compression pipeline for private installs. Installer upgrade operator now supports checkpointed, rollback-safe metric migrations. Feature off by default; enable with obs_shard_allocator in installer config. See docs/observability-sharding.md for details.
notes: Performance impact: initial benchmarks show 30-45% reduction in single-node TSDB growth at 8 shards; operational docs added. Airgapped fallback uses on-cluster CRD statestore. Follow-on work: autoscaler to rebalance shard sizes and a UI in Console for shard visualization.
